name: Algebra Flash
description: Algebra Flash 2.2 has just been released! Changelog: New gamemode! Thank you for the continued support of the game! Huh, is that it? Slightly disappointed, you boot up the game and click on the new gamemode. It says " Colored platforms ". There are $$$n$$$ platforms, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, placed one after another. There are $$$m$$$ colors available in the game, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$. The $$$i$$$-th platform is colored $$$c_i$$$. You start on the platform $$$1$$$ and want to reach platform $$$n$$$. In one move, you can jump from some platform $$$i$$$ to platforms $$$i + 1$$$ or $$$i + 2$$$. All platforms are initially deactivated (including platforms $$$1$$$ and $$$n$$$). For each color $$$j$$$, you can pay $$$x_j$$$ coins to activate all platforms of that color. You want to activate some platforms so that you could start on an activated platform $$$1$$$, jump through some activated platforms and reach an activated platform $$$n$$$. What's the smallest amount of coins you can spend to achieve that?
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$1 \le m \le 40$$$) — the number of platforms and the number of colors, respectively. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n$$$ ($$$1 \le c_i \le m$$$) — the colors of the platforms. The third line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_m$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i \le 10^7$$$) — the cost of activating all platforms of each color.
output_specification: Print the smallest amount of coins you can spend to activate some platforms so that you could start on an activated platform $$$1$$$, jump through some activated platforms and reach an activated platform $$$n$$$.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1767E — Algebra Flash [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
